subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bergmann's rule states that within a widely distributed warm-blooded species, populations living in colder climates tend to have larger body sizes than those in warmer climates.
• The rule attributes this pattern to the fact that larger bodies retain heat more efficiently because of a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio.
• Bergmann's rule, originally formulated for mammals and birds, has also been documented in some cold-tolerant reptile and fish species.
• Laura Ingram and Hendra Jang studied deer mouse populations across North America from 2015 to 2022.
• Deer mice from northern Canadian populations were notably larger in body size than deer mice from populations in the southern United States.
prompt: The student wants to provide an explanation and example of Bergmann's rule. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Northern Canadian deer mice are larger in body size than their southern counterparts, demonstrating Bergmann's rule, which describes the larger body sizes of warm-blooded animals in colder climates but applies to some reptiles and fish as well.
choices.B: Bergmann's rule states that warm-blooded species in colder climates tend to have larger body sizes than those in warmer climates; for example, many cold-climate animals are larger than their warm-climate relatives.
choices.C: Bergmann's rule, which describes the body-size patterns of deer mice and other warm-blooded animals, attributes the trend to the lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger bodies.
choices.D: Laura Ingram and Hendra Jang studied deer mouse populations across North America from 2015 to 2022, a clear example of Bergmann's rule, which describes the larger body sizes of warm-blooded animals in colder climates.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer. The sentence effectively explains Bergmann's rule by describing how warm-blooded animals in colder climates tend to have larger bodies, notes that the rule extends beyond mammals and birds to some reptiles and fish, and uses the specific finding that northern Canadian deer mice are larger than southern populations as a concrete example.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect. The sentence emphasizes the secondary detail about surface-area-to-volume ratio rather than focusing on the primary statement of the rule, and it does not provide a concrete example demonstrating the rule in action.
